description: E2 detection pack. Ground truth is authored here, by hand, and never inferred from the detector's output. Contains the four required structures: true collision, semantic duplicate (same purpose, different words), independent control (must not be flagged), and hidden dependency (a real collision no entity-overlap detector can see). Tuned to be HARD on purpose: a pack the detector passes tells us nothing, and the plan anticipates E2 failing first (trigger I3). Whether a proposal overlaps prior work is NOT declared here - the evaluator derives it from priorEvents and refuses to score a pack whose labels contradict its own events.

priorEvents.intentText: add jsonify helper to the view function
add jsonify helper for serialising dicts
make the endpoint hand back a JSON document instead of a rendered page
reuse the existing serialiser rather than writing another one
wire up make_response so the view returns structured output
limit make_response to a single call site
validate that the secret key is set before the app starts
add a rotating file handler for the request logger
add a shell command that prints the resolved configuration
narrow the config value type to a union

proposals.intentText: add a jsonify helper to the view
proposals.why: Same file and near-identical wording as T-shared-lexical. This is the case the lexical baseline is built to catch; failing it would mean the detector is broken rather than limited.
Same file, shares the make_response identifier. Identifier overlap is the strongest lexical signal available, so this must be caught.

proposals.intentText: return a JSON payload from the handler rather than HTML
proposals.why: The same purpose as T-dup-semantic, stated in different words. Shared entity makes it reachable, so a miss would be a genuine matcher limitation rather than a structural one. This is the hardest semantic case in the pack.

proposals.intentText: avoid duplicating the serializer by calling the existing helper
proposals.why: Same purpose as T-dup-semantic on the same file, with disjoint wording but the shared word serializer. Included to separate 'paraphrase' from 'paraphrase that happens to share a term', which decides whether I3 needs a better matcher or better intent capture.

proposals.intentText: add a context manager for the test client
proposals.why: Nobody else touched this file and the intent is unrelated. Must never be flagged: this is the false-positive floor, and the accuracy gate is meaningless without it.

proposals.intentText: support loading configuration from a TOML file
proposals.why: Overlaps T-control-same-entity on flask/config.py but for unrelated reasons: validity checking versus a new loader, sharing almost no content words. Counted as a false positive deliberately, per H9 - entity overlap alone is not evidence of a coordination failure. Under A3 this costs tokens only; under A4 it refuses legitimate work.

proposals.intentText: emit the config-loaded signal from the new accessor
proposals.why: Depends on T-hidden-upstream's change in flask/cli.py and flask/typing.py, and shares no entity with any in-flight work. A real collision that no entity-key detector can reach. Present to establish the recall ceiling rather than to score against it.

proposals.intentText: validate that the secret key is set before the app starts
proposals.why: Nearly the same wording as T-control-same-entity's change to flask/config.py, but on a file where nobody else is working. Guards the opposite error from the overlap control: text similarity must not be sufficient on its own when the entity is untouched.
